items.statement: In a microscopy study, damage at 60 °C was already visible when the coffee still held 20% moisture, while sun-dried coffee and coffee dried at 40 °C were undamaged at 11%.

sources.title: Microscopia eletrônica de varredura do endosperma de café (Coffea arabica L.) durante o processo de secagem
sources.quote: When dried at 60°C, changes in the cellular structures of the cytoplasm were observed for coffees with moisture content of 20%.

items.note: Saath et al. 2010 (Cienc. Agrotec. 34(1)), C. arabica, natural and pulped coffee pre-dried on a patio and then dried on the patio or in fixed-layer dryers at 40 and 60 °C down to 11% (wb). The abstract states that the cytoplasm at 11% was not affected by patio/sun or 40 °C drying, and that at 60 °C changes were seen in coffee at 20% moisture. Read from the abstract (UNESP/Sumarios records); the DOAJ link itself did not load and the full text was not opened.

items.statement: The 2017 textbook chapter reads the evidence the same way: shade helps quality most in sub-optimal, heat-stressed regions.

items.note: The Craft and Science of Coffee (2017), ch. 2, section 5.2: 'Shade appears to impart its greatest benefit in coffee bean flavor for plants growing in suboptimal and heat-stressed growing regions' (citing Muschler 2001), and later it calls this the likely reason for better quality in suboptimal conditions. The chapter's own framing matches the statement. The stored quote (leguminous tree genera) is not the passage the statement rests on.

sources.quote: ‘deforestation’ means the conversion of forest to agricultural use, whether human-induced or not;

The stored quote is the definition of deforestation (Art. 2), not this passage. The tool returned Art. 4(1) partly paraphrased, but the meaning is clear.

items.statement: It describes Australians as predominantly tea drinkers across all classes until the Second World War, Greek and Italian roasters setting up in the post-war decades, and espresso as known in 2010 established only late in the 20th century.

Greek and Italian roasters set up their businesses 'from the late 1950s on'. Espresso 'as we know it today was not established until the late 1970s and early 1980s'. 'Post-war decades' and 'late in the 20th century' are fair paraphrases.

The text adds that seed propagation of Arabica pure lines risks contamination by foreign pollen. This supports the statement. The stored quote (on in vitro skills) is from the next panel and is not the passage the statement rests on.

items.note: FAO X6939E Annex 10, Fig. 6, is one captioned photo of 'Wet processing system' that numbers receiving tank, siphon, pulper, separating screen, repasser (2nd pulper) and fermentation tanks. The caption names no country and does not call the system typical. The annex covers African countries in general, and only Fig. 14 is labelled Kenya. The sequence is supported, but 'typical East African' is not.
items.suggested_fix: A wet processing system pictured in an FAO report on post-harvest handling in African countries shows the order: receiving tank, siphon, pulper, separating screen, repasser (a second pulper), then fermentation tanks.

items.statement: Naming a coffee's acidity after one acid is therefore unreliable.

sources.title: Acids in Brewed Coffee: Chemical Composition and Sensory Threshold
sources.quote: Combined, the results question the direct relation between individual organic acids and acidity in coffee and point towards a more complex understanding of perceived acidity.

sources.title: A System to Assess Coffee Value: Understanding the Specialty Coffee Association’s Coffee Value Assessment (June 2024)
sources.quote: Unfortunately, we have no sensory references for terms such as “juicy acidity” or “bright acidity,” and the use of organic acids as references tends to be misleading, as coffees often have a mixture of many different organic acids.

items.note: The SCA document 'A System to Assess Coffee Value' (June 2024, local copy at papers/cup/SCA_CVA_Protocol_2024.txt, section 6.4) says organic acids used as references tend to mislead because coffees contain a mixture of many acids. It adds that a 'phosphoric acid' profile may hold little phosphoric acid and that a green-apple acidity is likely not malic acid. This supports the statement. The second source (s12, SSRN 4550010) could not be fetched and was not checked.

Rather it has developed a transnational community of fans'. Both halves of the statement are supported. The stored quote ('somewhat reductive') supports a different sentence.

items.statement: A 2013 study concludes that the resistance involves a set of defence responses, not only a hypersensitive reaction.

sources.title: Defense responses to Meloidogyne exigua in resistant coffee cultivar and non-host plant
sources.quote: The resistance of coffee plants to Meloidogyne exigua is conferred by the gene Mex-1.

items.note: Silva et al. 2013, Tropical Plant Pathology 38(2). Read via the UFV LOCUS record of the abstract only, because the SciELO page timed out on permission. The study compared susceptible C. arabica 'Catuaí' with the resistant C. canephora cultivar 'Apoatã' and a non-host plant. It concludes that 'the coffee cultivar's resistance to M. exigua is not restricted to HR' but includes constitutive and induced responses, mainly phenolic-like compounds. In the entry the sentence sits under 'Resistant arabica', right after Mex-1 in arabica (T5296), so it reads as a general claim about Mex-1 arabica resistance. The finding was shown in one C. canephora cultivar. The cultivar identity rests on the abstract summary; the full text was not read.
items.suggested_fix: A 2013 study of the resistant C. canephora cultivar Apoatã concludes that its resistance to M. exigua involves a set of constitutive and induced defence responses, not only a hypersensitive reaction.

items.note: SCA Water Quality Handbook ed. 2 (local copy, p. 29 and glossary) says only that a softener is an ion-exchange method where 'calcium and magnesium ions are exchanged for either sodium or potassium ions', reducing hardness without affecting alkalinity. items.suggested_fix: The resin exchanges the calcium and magnesium ions in the water for sodium or potassium ions, which lowers total hardness without changing alkalinity. (If the 2:1 ratio and the equation are kept, mark them as our addition from charge balance, or cite a chemistry source.)

items.statement: In the SCA handbook's reading, a swollen sealed bag or a deformed capsule means the coffee was packed before enough gas had left.

items.note: Local copy of the SCA Coffee Freshness Handbook, sec. 4.7.2: a bag sealed air-tight without a valve inflates during storage, and coffee must be off-gassed before it is packed in hermetically sealed bags.
